newsitem.title: UK: London freight sees some sign of more inquiry.
newsitem.headline: London freight sees some sign of more inquiry.

text.p: One leading grain broker reckoned that there was "more buzz in the market today" and although the situation remains generally grim for owners, especially of Capers, there was some evidence of more chartering enquiry.

Brokers pointed out that the availability of Panamaxes might become less abundant in the Pacific in particular, and there was significantly more chartering activity reported from the Lakes. But freight rates have yet to pick up and the Baltic Freight Inex lost three more points to 992.

A feature of the latest fixture lists has been the involvement of Chinese-controlled tonnage in the Atlantic Panamax heavy grain trades. These vessels have accounted for Bunge's 55,000 US Gulf/Rotterdam at a lumpsum equivalent of $8.00 for Oct 5/10, Continental's 50,000 US Gulf/Aqaba at $17.00 for Oct 1/7 and Halla's 54,000 US Gulf/Taiwan at $17.70 - all rates down on last fixed.

Hanjin are reported to have fixed Halla tonnage for 54,000 US Gulf/Japan for Oct 15/28 at $18.75 no combo (Dreyfus paid $19.00 yesterday) but Cargill were rumoured not to have seen tonnage anywhere near these low levels for their new US Gulf/Japan order today for up to 55,000 tonnes for Oct 18/25.

Other new Panamax enquiries included Lalemant 55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Holland-Belgium for Oct 15/30 and Katrina 54,000 US Gulf/Japan for Oct 21/30. Brokers expect rates to come off the bottom for early Oct loading in the North Pacific where Dreyfus still quote Panamax grain business to Sri Lanka and Continental have orders to both Japan and Taiwan.

Transfield are reported to have fixed Captain George l 64,000 dwt on subjects NoPac/China at $6,000 daily plus $100,000 bonus and Shadab may have fixed Stone Gemini for grain from Australia. Brokers report a clear-out of early Panamaxes in the East. Handy-Size business has been active in the Lakes and St Lawrence with Cargill said to have booked 18-25,000 wheat to Callao at $27.00/20.00 and polish tonnage Lakes/Italy at $29.25.

Conti Latin fixed 31,300 heavy grain US Gulf/Buenaventura for Oct 3/10 at $14.50. Some new enquiry was quoted for Handies including 20,000 pellets by Holbud up river to Indonesia and 30,000 wheat St Lawrence/Turkey by Toepfer.

Most brokers describe prospects for Capers as bleak with thin forward enquiry. Panamaxes seem to be in better demand. Coal business is reported fixed by Luigi Dmato 75,300 dwt to Japanese charterers E Australia/Japan at $7,250 daily plus $100,000 bonus and Otterpool to van Ommeren for 55,000 Roberts Bank/Constanza, possibly at just over $10.00.

Bright State 68,676 dwt has been linked with Armada basis prompt delivery Far East for short timecharter period at $7,600 daily, and Titus 62,180 dwt with Pan Ocean for a NoPac round on private terms. Kleimar are said to have booked 55,000/10 bauxite Weipa/Pto Vesme at d9.25. The Indian government fixed Pisc Trader 41,796 dwt for bulk coking coal from E Australia to E Coast India on private terms. In the Atlantic Transworld 73,000 dwt was believed taken by Pan Ocean from Ubu to Cigading at $10,000 daily plus unknown bonus.

Weak fixtures from the Continent were rumoured to have been completed by Alpha Faith 37,000 dwt for a transatlantic round to Van Ommeren and by Hemlock 29,288 dwt to the Arabian Gulf, but full details were lacking. Lakes chartering has sprung to lifeith at least 3 vessels fixed for rounds with Oct delivery on the Continent, all at between $7,000 and 8,000 daily.

In the East Major Basil 27,000 dwt fixed a short CIS trip at close to $5,000 daily and Furness Withy booked the Seanav-relet Beta Navis 39,000 dwt delivery Taiwan trip via Australia to the Continent at about $4,500 daily. K Line fixed a Chinese 45,000 dwt craned bulker USWC/Continent with bauxite on private terms.
